title: WhatsApp back
description:
Revive the legacy `whatsappData` pattern from `@src/conversations/flow/conversations-flows.ts` for agent-driven messages, but move the configuration ownership into each agent tool.

Current verified state:
- Legacy conversation flows already carry `whatsappData` inside `ConversationFlowModel`, and `NotificationsService` dispatches WhatsApp messages based on that shape (`sendsNotification`, `ignoresTemplate`, `templateUsesMessageAsParam`) in `@src/notifications/notifications.service.ts`.
- Agent results currently get converted into synthetic conversation flows in `ConversationsService.convertAgentResultToFlow()`, where flow ids are derived from tool names as `agent.tool.${toolName}`.
- `ToolResult` already carries `message`, completion metadata, and a `flowId`, but agent-originated WhatsApp metadata is not yet propagated into the stored assistant flow/message.
- `NotificationsModule` already depends on `WhatsAppModule`, and the WhatsApp side is intentionally thin: it accepts a stored assistant flow and decides whether to send text/interactive/template variants.

Target outcome:
- Extend the agent tool contract so each tool can emit WhatsApp delivery metadata alongside its normal message response.
- Standardise agent flow ids/tool ids so WhatsApp template mapping is deterministic and stable, rather than inferred ad hoc from `currentTool`.
- Preserve the existing thin WhatsApp notification layer by reusing the current `ConversationFlowWhatsappData`-style shape where possible.
- Ensure agent-produced assistant messages are stored as `ConversationFlowModel` values that include WhatsApp metadata, so `NotificationsService.dispatchAssistantMessages()` can continue to work with minimal change.
- Document the operational implications for WhatsApp templates and session-window behaviour in `@docs/WHATSAPP_SETUP.md`.

Implementation direction:
1. Define a standard agent-side WhatsApp config contract, ideally aligned with the existing `ConversationFlowWhatsappData` model rather than inventing a second shape.
2. Extend `ToolResult` / `AbstractTool.createResponse()` so tools can emit this metadata explicitly.
3. Introduce a standardised agent flow/tool id scheme and make `ConversationsService.convertAgentResultToFlow()` use it directly instead of reconstructing ids from `currentTool`.
4. Update agent tools incrementally to declare their WhatsApp behaviour near the message they produce.
5. Keep the notifications/WhatsApp layer thin by consuming the propagated metadata from stored assistant messages, only adding a small compatibility layer if agent outputs need normalization.
6. Add focused tests around flow conversion, notification dispatch, and any template-name mapping for agent-originated flows.
7. Follow `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md` for all code and test changes. New behaviour in this story must be covered with automated tests, with unit/service tests kept atomic, dependencies mocked, and happy-path plus compatibility/error scenarios explicitly covered.

Important design constraints:
- Avoid duplicating WhatsApp message-routing logic between agent tools and `NotificationsService`; tools should declare intent, notifications should execute delivery.
- Keep backwards compatibility for legacy conversation flows that already use `whatsappData`.
- Prefer one shared WhatsApp metadata shape across legacy flows and agent tools.
- Do not couple individual agent tools directly to WhatsApp services or modules; metadata should flow through `ToolResult` and persisted conversation messages.
- Standardised ids must be stable enough to support WhatsApp template naming via the existing `flowId -> template` conversion.
- All new code and tests in this story must adhere to `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md`, including near-complete coverage expectations for changed paths and atomic service-level tests with mocked dependencies.

features.title: Standardise agent flow ids and WhatsApp metadata in ToolResult / AbstractTool
features.description:
Define a single agent-side contract for WhatsApp delivery metadata and stable flow ids.

Scope:
- Update `@src/agent/tools/base/base-tool.interface.ts` so `ToolResult` can carry WhatsApp metadata using the same semantics as legacy `ConversationFlowWhatsappData` (`sendsNotification`, `ignoresTemplate`, `templateUsesMessageAsParam`).
- Update `@src/agent/tools/base/base-tool.abstract.ts` so `createResponse()` can emit that metadata consistently without each tool reimplementing the shape.
- Standardise `flowId` generation for agent tools so it is explicit and stable, instead of relying on `ConversationsService` to derive `agent.tool.${toolName}` from `currentTool`.
- Decide and document whether `flowId` should always be required for agent tool responses that might trigger WhatsApp templates.
- Follow `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md`; keep the contract small, cohesive, and easy to unit test.

Testing requirements:
- Add/extend unit tests alongside `@src/agent/tools/base/base-tool.interface.ts` / `@src/agent/tools/base/base-tool.abstract.ts` changed behaviour.
- Tests should be atomic and verify one code path per test, with mocked dependencies only.
- Cover happy path, omitted WhatsApp metadata, and stable `flowId` behaviour.

Acceptance:
- Agent tools have a first-class way to declare WhatsApp delivery intent.
- A stable flow id scheme exists for all agent tool outputs.
- The WhatsApp metadata shape is shared with legacy flow semantics rather than duplicated.
- Contract changes are covered by automated tests aligned with project testing standards.

features.title: Propagate agent WhatsApp metadata into stored assistant conversation flows
features.description:
Update the conversation bridge so agent outputs become stored assistant flows that already contain the WhatsApp configuration needed by notifications.

Scope:
- Refactor `@src/conversations/conversations.service.ts`, especially `convertAgentResultToFlow()`, to use the tool-provided `flowId` directly when present.
- Copy agent WhatsApp metadata from `ToolResult` into the produced `ConversationFlowModel` so the persisted assistant message contains `whatsappData`.
- Preserve existing fallback behaviour for legacy or incomplete agent responses, but avoid reconstructing ids when a standard id is available.
- Ensure any inputs/buttons/suggested prompts needed by WhatsApp interactive sends remain available on the stored assistant flow.
- Follow `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md`; keep the conversion logic focused and testable.

Testing requirements:
- Add/extend atomic service tests for `@src/conversations/conversations.service.ts`, preferably using the existing conversation test helpers where appropriate.
- Mock all dependencies and cover happy path, fallback compatibility, and missing/partial agent metadata scenarios.
- Verify stored flow ids, propagated `whatsappData`, and preservation of any interactive data needed by notifications.

Acceptance:
- Agent-originated assistant messages are stored with stable ids and WhatsApp metadata.
- `NotificationsService.dispatchAssistantMessages()` can operate on agent-generated messages with minimal or no special casing.
- Legacy conversation flows continue to work unchanged.
- Changed paths are covered by automated tests aligned with project testing standards.

features.title: Keep NotificationsService as a thin delivery layer for legacy and agent flows
features.description:
Preserve the existing WhatsApp dispatch model while adding only the minimal normalization needed for agent-originated messages.

Scope:
- Review `@src/notifications/notifications.service.ts` and confirm the existing dispatch contract can serve both legacy and agent-generated assistant messages.
- If needed, add only a small compatibility layer for agent outputs, without moving decision logic out of conversation/tool layers.
- Ensure template naming still derives deterministically from flow ids via `convertFlowToTemplate()`.
- Validate that interactive messages still depend on `inputsData` and that agent-originated flows can opt into that path where appropriate.
- Follow `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md`; keep business logic centralised and service boundaries clean.

Testing requirements:
- Extend `@src/notifications/notifications.service.spec.ts` with atomic service tests for both legacy and agent-originated assistant messages.
- Mock all WhatsApp/outbound dependencies; never call real providers.
- Cover text send, interactive send, template send, compatibility fallback, and no-send cases.

Acceptance:
- Notification dispatch logic stays centralised and thin.
- No tool or conversation code calls WhatsApp services directly.
- Both legacy flows and agent flows share the same delivery pipeline and template naming rules.
- Delivery-path changes are covered by automated tests aligned with project testing standards.

features.title: Add WhatsApp configuration to agent tools incrementally
features.description:
Move message-specific WhatsApp behaviour out of the legacy central flow list and into the relevant agent tools.

Scope:
- Inspect agent tools that currently correspond to WhatsApp-triggered journeys (for example morning check-in, evening check-in, journal, weekly review, momentum, micro goals, check-in times, onboarding).
- For each tool, declare the appropriate stable flow ids and WhatsApp metadata near the response creation site.
- Reuse the legacy behaviour where it already exists in `@src/conversations/flow/conversations-flows.ts` as the source of truth for initial parity.
- Identify which tools should send notifications, which should ignore templates, and which should use message text as a template param.
- Follow `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md`; keep tool responsibilities local, explicit, and unit-testable.

Testing requirements:
- Extend the relevant existing tool specs as each tool is migrated.
- Keep tests atomic with mocked collaborators only; do not test unrelated phases in the same case.
- Cover at least one happy path plus one compatibility/default path per migrated tool where WhatsApp metadata is introduced.

Acceptance:
- WhatsApp-related behaviour is owned by the tools that emit the messages.
- Behaviour matches or intentionally replaces legacy `whatsappData` semantics.
- The legacy flow file is no longer the long-term source of WhatsApp config for agent-driven messages.
- Each migrated tool change is covered by automated tests aligned with project testing standards.

features.title: Document and test agent-originated WhatsApp delivery
features.description:
Cover the new contract with documentation and focused tests.

Scope:
- Add/extend tests around `@src/conversations/conversations.service.ts` for agent result to flow conversion, especially stable flow ids and `whatsappData` propagation.
- Extend `@src/notifications/notifications.service.spec.ts` to include agent-originated assistant messages and verify text/interactive/template dispatch paths.
- Update `@docs/WHATSAPP_SETUP.md` to explain that WhatsApp templates and out-of-session routing now depend on stable agent flow ids as well as legacy flow ids.
- Document any constraints on template naming, id format, and when `templateUsesMessageAsParam` should be used.
- Explicitly follow `@docs/CODE_STANDARD.md` and `@docs/TESTING.md` for all documentation, code, and test updates in this feature.

Testing requirements:
- Keep service tests atomic, with mocked dependencies and explicit assertions per delivery branch.
- Cover happy path plus compatibility/error scenarios, including missing metadata and stable template-name derivation.
- Ensure changed files meet the project's near-complete coverage expectations for touched logic.

Acceptance:
- Tests lock down the new propagation path end to end at the service level.
- Docs explain the operational impact of stable agent flow ids for WhatsApp templates.
- Regressions between legacy flow messages and agent messages are easier to catch.
- Documentation and tests are aligned with project code/testing standards.
